The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Kemparaju, in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.02.2023.
2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:

On 25.02.2023 at about 6.15 p.m. the deceased Kemparaju was proceeding as pedestrian on the extreme side of Kanakapura- Bengaluru road, when he reached near Rice mill, NH-209 road, Kanakapura at that time the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-KA-1975 has ridden the same from Kanakapura side towards Jayalakshmamma vs Jagannath.

Bengaluru in a rash and negligent manner and dashed  SCCH-17 4 MVC No. 1618-2023 against the deceased.
Due to the impact he sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to General Hospital, Kanakapura after first aid he was shifted to CDSIMER, Dr. Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital and later he was shifted to NIMHANS wherein he was admitted as inpatient, but in spite of best treatment he succumbed to the said injuries on 01.3.2023.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, funeral and other incidental expenses.
At the time of accident, the deceased was working as carpentry and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. he was contributing his entire income to his family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically.
The petitioners No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 to 4 are the major daughters of the deceased Kemparjau, have lost love and affection

The respondents are the owner and insurer of the vehicle are liable to pay compensation compensation to the petitioners.

2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are  the legal heirs and dependents of  deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation?
If so, what amount and  from whom?

It is the contention of respondent No.1 & 2 that even though the rider of bike bearing No  SCCH-17 11 MVC No. 1618-2023 KA-05-KA-1975 are proceeding slowly by following the traffic rules, the victim/ deceased was crossing the main road without their being any crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights and that too in the main Jayalakshmamma vs Jagannath.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146827261/

12. If we perused the contents of Ex.P5 spot mahazar along with the evidence lead by the petitioner the accident is happened in the left side of the road within the seven feet from the left side edge of the road.
The Ex.P5 mahazar and the rough sketch appended to Ex.P5  SCCH-17 12 MVC No. 1618-2023 depicts that from the accident spot to road divider, there is 21 feet distance is available.
Thus, it can be construed that the accident is happened in the left side of the road and it shows that the deceased was trying to cross the road and was not in the middle of the road.
It is very important to note that as stated by the respondents the accident is not in the middle of the road, but as per the rough sketch it is in the left side of the road.
It is very important to note at this point that the rider of bike bearing No. KA-05-KA-1975 who came in the left side of the road dashed against the deceased.

Thus, it can be construed that the rider of the bike bearing No. KA-05- Jayalakshmamma vs Jagannath.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146827261/

13. It is very important to note that the accident place is in the main road.

Thus the learned counsel for  SCCH-17 13 MVC No. 1618-2023 the respondent No.2 taken contention that in the main road the deceased was trying to cross the road where there is no crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights.
Admittedly the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the existence of crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights in the accident spot.
In the same manner the respondents also not adduced any evidence in support of their contentions by showing that there is no crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights in the accident spot.
Thus if we perused the contents of rough sketch, there is no pedestrian crossing in the accident spot or near to the accident spot.

Thus,
it is very impractical to expect that the deceased would have been crossed the road only in pedestrian crossing.
When there is no crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights in the roads the pedestrians can cross the  SCCH-17 14 MVC No. 1618-2023 main road with a caution and being vigilant.

In this case,
the accident spot is in the left side of the road thus, it cannot be construed as the deceased was negligent and Jayalakshmamma vs Jagannath.C on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146827261/

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Hence, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-KA-1975. are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.

The petitioners are entitle for the compensation along with the interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

Accordingly, Issue No.3 answered partly in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.4:-

36 . For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.11,70,600/-(Rupees Eleven lakhs Seventy thousand six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitle for the compensation awarded under the head of loss of consortium i.e., Rs.44,000/- each along with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the realization of said amount from respondents.
Considering the quantum of award it is order to release the entire amount to the petitioner Nos. 2 to 4.

In the remaining total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners, 50% of compensation shall be released in favour petitioner No.1, on her proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in her name.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Kemparaju, in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.02.2023.
Further contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of deceased himself.
She has denied the age,
avocation and income of the petitioner.
Hence, the  SCCH-17 6 MVC No. 1618-2023 respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against him.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of insurance policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-05- KA-1975.
and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that the rider of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
The accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased and there is no negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle.
It has denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:

 Bengaluru- Kanakapura road, Kanakapura  town and taluk, Ramanagara District, due  to the rash and negligence driving of the  motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-KA-1975 by  its rider?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are  the legal heirs and dependents of  deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation?
If so, what amount and  from whom?
4 . What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus the learned counsel for  SCCH-17 13 MVC No. 1618-2023 the respondent No.2 taken contention that in the main road the deceased was trying to cross the road where there is no crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights.
Admittedly the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the existence of crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights in the accident spot.
In the same manner the respondents also not adduced any evidence in support of their contentions by showing that there is no crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights in the accident spot.
Thus if we perused the contents of rough sketch, there is no pedestrian crossing in the accident spot or near to the accident spot.
Thus,
it is very impractical to expect that the deceased would have been crossed the road only in pedestrian crossing.
When there is no crossing zone, zebra crossing and no signal lights in the roads the pedestrians can cross the  SCCH-17 14 MVC No. 1618-2023 main road with a caution and being vigilant.
In this case,

 In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have  considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to  supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and  recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in  the affirmative.
